subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the main difference between a function and a procedure?
options: They are identical in every way
A procedure always returns a value; a function never does
A function returns a value; a procedure does not have to
questions.explain: A function returns a value to the calling code, whereas a procedure need not.

questions.q: What does the modulo (MOD) operator return?
options: The whole-number result of a division
questions.explain: The MOD operator returns the remainder left after an integer division.

questions.q: In a database table, what is a record?
options: A row containing data about one item or entity
questions.explain: A record is a row that holds all the data about one item/entity.

questions.q: What is the difference between a variable and a constant?
options: Both can change freely at any time
A variable's value can change while a program runs; a constant's value does not
A constant can change but a variable cannot
questions.explain: A variable can change value during execution, whereas a constant stays the same.

questions.q: What type of error is a logic error?
options: An error caused by faulty hardware
The code runs but produces incorrect results
The code will not run because rules of the language are broken
An error in the network connection
questions.explain: A logic error lets the program run but produces incorrect or unintended results.

questions.q: What is a parameter in a subroutine?
options: A value passed into the subroutine for it to use
The result a subroutine sends back
questions.explain: A parameter is a value passed into a subroutine for it to use.

questions.q: What does the Boolean operator AND require to return True?
options: Only the first condition must be True
At least one condition must be True
questions.explain: AND returns True only when both conditions are True.

questions.q: A WHILE loop is best described as:
options: A way of selecting between two options
A subroutine that returns a value
A loop that repeats while a condition is True (condition-controlled)
A loop that always runs exactly ten times
questions.explain: A WHILE loop is condition-controlled, repeating as long as its condition is True.

questions.q: Which is an advantage of a high-level language over a low-level language?
options: It is easier for humans to read and write
questions.explain: High-level languages are easier for humans to understand and write than low-level languages.

questions.q: Which data type would best store the value True or False?
questions.explain: A Boolean stores one of two values: True or False.

questions.q: What is the purpose of input validation?
options: To check that data entered is sensible and acceptable before it is used
To connect the program to the internet
To translate the program into machine code
To make the program run faster
questions.explain: Input validation checks that entered data is reasonable/acceptable before processing.

questions.q: In SQL, which command retrieves data from a database?
questions.explain: The SQL SELECT statement retrieves (queries) data from a database.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a compiler and an interpreter?
options: Both translate the whole program before running
An interpreter translates the whole program at once; a compiler runs line by line
A compiler translates the whole program at once; an interpreter translates and runs line by line
questions.explain: A compiler translates all the code at once, while an interpreter translates and executes line by line.

questions.q: Boundary test data is used to:
options: Test values at the edges of the accepted range
questions.explain: Boundary test data checks values right at the edges of the valid range.

questions.q: Which construct repeats a block of code a set number of times?
questions.explain: A FOR loop is count-controlled iteration that repeats a set number of times.

questions.q: Given the array scores = [10, 20, 30, 40], what does scores[1] hold (zero-indexed)?
questions.explain: With zero-based indexing, scores[1] is the second element, 20.

questions.q: What does the Boolean operator OR return when both conditions are False?
options: It depends on the first condition only
questions.explain: OR returns True if at least one condition is True, so with both False it returns False.

questions.q: Which data type best stores a number with a decimal point, such as 3.14?
questions.explain: A real (float) data type stores numbers with a fractional/decimal part.

questions.q: Which data type best stores a whole number such as 42?
questions.explain: An integer stores a whole number.

questions.q: If the string 'COMPUTER' is held in a variable, what would a substring command extracting positions 0 to 2 typically return?
questions.explain: Taking characters from index 0 up to 2 returns the first three letters, 'COM'.

questions.q: Which programming construct is used for selection?
questions.explain: Selection is implemented using IF (and ELSE) statements to choose between paths.

questions.q: Which of these is a syntax error?
options: The loop runs one time too few
The program gives the wrong average due to a + used instead of *
A missing closing bracket that stops the code running
The output is in the wrong order
questions.explain: A syntax error breaks the rules of the language (e.g. a missing bracket) and stops the code running.
